text.title: Two-pass: free reasoning then strict extraction
text.summary: Run hard reasoning in free text on the strong model, then extract into the strict schema with a cheap model.

section.title: The rule
section.p: For tasks where reasoning quality matters more than output format, never lock the reasoning step into strict structured output. Split the work into two passes: pass 1 produces free-form reasoning on the strong model, pass 2 extracts the structured answer with a cheap model.

rule.statement: When a task requires deep reasoning AND a strict schema, run the strong model in free-text or extended-thinking mode for the reasoning step, then run a cheap extractor model with strict structured output to fill the schema from the strong model's transcript.
rule.rationale: Corrected 2026-08-04. The cost is the FORMAT INSTRUCTION in the prompt, not the grammar mask: The Format Tax (arXiv:2604.03616, 2026-04-04) separates the format request from the constrained decode and finds 92 percent of statistically significant degradations already present with the instruction alone, before any decoder constraint. A format instruction compresses the visible reasoning channel before the model has finished solving, so it commits early. Two-pass restores accuracy — +6.8 pp on average, improving 42 of 72 model x task x format combinations — because pass 1 sees no format request at all, and the extraction step is easy enough that a small model meets the spec at a fraction of the cost. Earlier SLOT / vendor-guide figures of 10–15 percent describe the combined effect and do not isolate the cause.

example.code:
# Pass 1: Opus thinks freely. raw = anthropic.messages.create( model="claude-opus-4-7", thinking={"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 16000}, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": question}], ).content[-1].text
# Pass 2: Haiku extracts into strict schema. verdict = haiku.responses.parse( model="claude-haiku-4-7", input=[{"role": "user", "content": f"Extract verdict from analysis:\n{raw}"}], text_format=Verdict, # strict Pydantic model )
example.note: Reasoning is unconstrained and benefits from extended thinking. Note what the prompt does NOT contain: no schema, no "reply as JSON", no field list — removing the decoder constraint while leaving the format instruction keeps almost the whole cost. Extraction is mechanical, so a Haiku-class model meets the schema reliably and cheaply.

example.code: # Single pass: Opus forced into strict JSON during reasoning. verdict = anthropic.messages.create( model="claude-opus-4-7", tools=[{"name": "submit_verdict", "input_schema": Verdict.model_json_schema()}], tool_choice={"type": "tool", "name": "submit_verdict"}, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": question}], )
example.note: Two problems, and the smaller one is the grammar. The schema is described to the model in the same turn it must reason in, which is where 92 percent of the measured degradation lives (arXiv:2604.03616, 2026-04-04); the decoder mask on top adds little further harm. Frontier closed models absorb most of this tax, so measure before assuming the loss.

antipattern.description: Adding a long reasoning field to a strict schema as a substitute for two-pass on math or research tasks.
antipattern.reason: The embedded scratchpad pattern works for medium-difficulty reasoning, but the schema is still stated up front, so the format instruction is still compressing the reasoning channel on the hard tasks — the scratchpad field does not undo that. The hidden-scratchpad variant (extended thinking, then format) recovers +9.2 pp on average but worsens 15 percent of combinations; two-pass is the lower-variance choice. When task difficulty saturates the scratchpad, switch to two-pass.
